Removing proline at a turn/helix-capping position is a classic destabilization strategy.

stop_reason.detail: Three orthogonal evidence sources consistently support the top 3 with clear separation from alternatives; remaining available tools cannot provide additional discriminative information for this destabilization objective.

history.rationale: Tryptophan at position 17 is a large hydrophobic residue likely buried in the core of the ferredoxin-like fold; mutation to charged Asp should severely destabilize the hydrophobic core.
Trp-to-Asp replaces a large buried hydrophobic/aromatic with a charged residue, highly likely to disrupt hydrophobic core packing and folding.

While MSA and PLM support disruption (z=0.000 for both), ProteinMPNN gives z=0.675 indicating moderate structural compatibility, suggesting the backbone can partially accommodate this substitution, reducing destabilization potential.
Leucine 11 is likely a core hydrophobic residue in the beta-sandwich; introducing a charged Asp in the core is highly destabilizing.
Leu-to-Asp introduces a charge into a likely hydrophobic region, expected to destabilize the fold.

All three tools support destabilization: ProteinMPNN z=0.156 (very incompatible), MSA frequency 0.000, ESM-1v z=0.0001. Introducing a charged residue at a conserved hydrophobic core position should disrupt folding.
Phenylalanine 40 is likely a core packing residue; mutation to charged Asp disrupts hydrophobic core interactions.
Phe-to-Asp disrupts aromatic/hydrophobic interactions with a charged substitution.
Structure (z=0.201) and PLM (z=0.000) strongly support destabilization, but MSA shows D at 19% of homologs at position 40, suggesting some evolutionary tolerance that weakens the disruption argument.
Proline 35 likely stabilizes a turn or loop in the ferredoxin fold; removing it disrupts backbone conformation and local structure.
Pro-to-Ala removes backbone conformational constraint, potentially disrupting a turn or loop critical for folding.

Phenylalanine 48 is likely buried in the hydrophobic core; substitution with charged Asp introduces electrostatic penalty in a nonpolar environment.
Phe-to-Asp at position 48 introduces charge where hydrophobic packing is expected.
ProteinMPNN z=0.802 indicates high structural compatibility and PLM z=0.012 shows some plausibility; MSA has low applicability (0.47). Overall poor support for destabilization.
Isoleucine 10 is likely part of the hydrophobic core; mutation to charged Asp is strongly destabilizing.
Ile-to-Asp replaces hydrophobic with charged residue, likely destabilizing.
MSA and PLM support disruption, but ProteinMPNN z=0.754 indicates the structure is quite compatible with this substitution, suggesting it may not effectively destabilize the fold.
Valine 36 is likely a core residue adjacent to the proline turn; mutation to Asp destabilizes the hydrophobic interior.
Val-to-Asp introduces charge in a hydrophobic context, expected to be destabilizing.
